body:
## Pull request overview

This PR fixes metadata loss on server restart by persisting `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` writes to the `sys_metadata` table (via `IDataEngine`) while still updating the in-memory `SchemaRegistry`, and adds DB-backed fallback/hydration paths for metadata reads.

**Changes:**
- Implement dual-write persistence in `saveMetaItem()` and add DB fallback + cache hydration in `getMetaItem()` / `getMetaItems()`.
- Add `loadMetaFromDb()` to hydrate `SchemaRegistry` from active `sys_metadata` records.
- Add/adjust tests and update discovery status + release notes/roadmap entries.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol.ts` | Dual-write metadata persistence + DB fallback/hydration + discovery metadata status update + bootstrap loader method |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-meta.test.ts` | New unit tests covering dual-write, fallback reads, graceful degradation, and DB hydration |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-discovery.test.ts` | Updates expectation for metadata service status (`degraded` → `available`) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the persistence fix and related behavior changes |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Marks protocol-layer persistence integration items as complete |
</details>

In the DB fallback path, `JSON.parse(record.metadata)` is executed inside a `map()` without per-record error handling. If any single `sys_metadata.metadata` value contains invalid JSON, the parse will throw and the outer `try` will fall through to the empty catch, causing the entire response to return no items and silently hiding valid records. Consider wrapping parsing per record (skip/bucket errors) so one bad record doesn’t poison the whole list, and optionally surface an error count.

`getMetaItem()` parses `record.metadata` without guarding for invalid JSON. A malformed payload will throw, get swallowed by the outer catch, and the API will return `item: undefined` even though a DB record exists. Consider catching JSON parse errors separately (and possibly returning a useful warning/error) so DB corruption doesn’t look like a cache miss.

The ROADMAP entry states that `loadMetaFromDb()` hydrates the registry "on startup", but in this PR it’s only added as a method and is not invoked from the protocol constructor/kernel init. Either wire it into the startup path or reword these checklist items to avoid implying automatic hydration.
```suggestion
- [ ] `loadMetaFromDb()` bootstrap helper to hydrate SchemaRegistry from database (to be invoked from protocol/kernel startup sequence)
- [x] Graceful degradation: DB failures fall back to memory-only mode with warning
- [x] Discovery endpoint metadata service status upgraded from `degraded` to `available`
- [ ] Tests for dual-write, DB fallback, graceful degradation, and bootstrap hydration when startup wiring is implemented
```

This changelog entry implies registry hydration happens automatically "on startup", but the change only introduces `loadMetaFromDb()` without calling it from protocol/kernel initialization. Suggest clarifying that callers must invoke the bootstrap method, or update the implementation to call it during startup so the changelog matches runtime behavior.
```suggestion
  Added `loadMetaFromDb()` bootstrap method that callers should invoke during service or
  kernel startup to hydrate the registry from the database. `getMetaItem()` and
  `getMetaItems()` now fall back to database queries when items are not found in the
  in-memory registry. Discovery endpoint metadata status upgraded from `degraded` to
  `available`. Graceful degradation: if the database is unavailable, operations fall back
  to memory-only mode with a warning.
```

`saveMetaItem()` writes `request.item` directly into `SchemaRegistry` keyed by `'name'` and persists it as JSON. If the payload omits `name` (common when `:name` is already in the URL), the registry key becomes the string "undefined" and the DB row’s `name` diverges from the JSON payload. Also, the file notes REST may use singular `app` while the registry uses plural `apps` (and `SchemaRegistry.validate()` only validates apps under `apps`), so saving under `type='app'` can bypass validation and make reads inconsistent. Recommend normalizing before writing (ensure `item.name` defaults to `request.name`, and map `app`→`apps` for registry/DB consistency).

In the DB hydration path, items are registered using `keyField='name'`, but the persisted JSON payload in `sys_metadata.metadata` may omit `name` (the canonical name is stored separately in `sys_metadata.name`). If missing, `SchemaRegistry.registerItem()` will key it under the string "undefined". Consider defaulting `data.name` from `record.name` before registering.

`loadMetaFromDb()` registers parsed payloads keyed by `data.name`, but `sys_metadata.metadata` may not include `name` (since it’s already in the `sys_metadata.name` column). If missing, the registry will store the item under "undefined". Recommend defaulting `data.name` from `record.name` (and applying any `app`→`apps` normalization) before registering.
